title: Doubled and Missing Number
statement:
An array nums of length n was supposed to hold each number from 1 to n exactly once, in some order. One mistake happened: one number was overwritten by a copy of another. So one value now appears twice and one value is missing.

Return [doubled, missing], in that order.

examples.why: The missing value can be 1, and the doubled value need not be next to it.
The array is not sorted, so you cannot just look for a gap between neighbours.

constraints: Exactly one value appears twice and exactly one value from 1..n is absent
hints: You know exactly which values should be there: 1 to n. What tells you how many times each one actually shows up?
A count array of size n + 1 answers both questions in one pass: the value with count 2 and the value with count 0.
For O(1) extra space: compare the actual sum with 1 + … + n, and do the same with the sum of squares. Two equations, two unknowns.

explain.intuition:
The range of values is known in advance, so a plain array of counts indexed by value is a perfect hash map. After one pass over nums, the value counted twice is the duplicate and the value counted zero times is the missing one.

A neat alternative uses arithmetic. Let d be the doubled value and m the missing one. The actual sum minus the expected sum is d − m. The same with squares gives d² − m² = (d − m)(d + m). Divide the two and you have d + m, then solve.
steps: Scan v from 1 to n: count[v] == 2 gives the doubled value, count[v] == 0 gives the missing one.
pitfalls: Sorting and reporting the first gap. If the missing value is 1 or n there is no gap between neighbours, as in [2, 2].
Returning the pair in the wrong order. The doubled value comes first.
Using only the plain sum. It gives d − m but not each value; you need a second equation or a count.

complexity.space: O(n), or O(1) with the sum trick

solutions.title: Count each value by scanning
solutions.idea: For every v from 1 to n, scan the array to count it.

solutions.title: Count array
solutions.idea: Values are 1..n, so an array indexed by value counts them in one pass.

solutions.title: Sum and sum of squares
solutions.idea: The sums give d − m and d² − m². Dividing gives d + m, and the two linear equations give both values.

followups: Solve it in O(1) extra space without big sums, by marking visited values as negative inside the array.
How would XOR find the pair, and what extra step tells you which of the two values is the duplicate?
